# Drawer

overlays · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen: filters, navigation, a list to pick
from on a phone. A swipe toward its edge closes it, and so does the x it always ends with.

```ts
import {
  DrawerBody, DrawerClose, DrawerDescription, DrawerFooter, DrawerHeader, DrawerPopup,
  DrawerRoot, DrawerTitle, DrawerTrigger,
} from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<DrawerRoot>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline">Filters</Button>} />
  <DrawerPopup>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Narrow the list of projects.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerBody>Status, owner and date.</DrawerBody>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline">Reset</Button>} />
      <DrawerClose render={<Button>Apply</Button>} />
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerPopup>
</DrawerRoot>
```

- **Parts.** Nine flat names and no bare `Drawer`: `DrawerRoot`, `DrawerTrigger`,
  `DrawerPopup`, `DrawerHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerBody`,
  `DrawerFooter` and `DrawerClose`. Each part passes the rest of its props to the element
  it draws. `DrawerRoot` draws none.
- **Placement.** `placement` on `DrawerRoot`: `end` (the default), `start`, `top` or
  `bottom`. `start` is the left in English and the right in Arabic. Never `left` or `right`.
- **Size.** `size` on `DrawerRoot` is the widest a `start` or `end` sheet grows: 256, 288,
  320, 384 or 480 px. `custom` sets no width; give `DrawerPopup` one with `className`.
- **Top and bottom.** They span the screen and grow to nine tenths of its height.
  A bottom sheet starts with a grabber.
- **The x.** Every sheet ends with a close button, and nothing removes it: a swipe is a
  drag, and a drag needs a second way (WCAG 2.5.7).
- **Swipe.** A swipe toward the sheet's own edge closes it, once it is past half of the
  sheet. A finger starts anywhere on the sheet; a mouse starts on the header.
- **Scrolling.** `DrawerBody` scrolls. The header and the footer stay put. In a bottom
  sheet a pull down from the top of the list moves the sheet, as on a phone.
- **Start with a header.** `DrawerHeader` keeps the title clear of the x. With no header,
  whatever comes first in the sheet ends 64 px short of that edge instead.
- **Labels.** Two forms work, on `DrawerTrigger` and on `DrawerClose`:
  `render={<Button>Filters</Button>}`, and `render={<Button />}` with `Filters` as children.
  On a server page only the first keeps the ellipsis of a long label, so the demos use it.
- **Disabled.** `disabled` on `DrawerTrigger` or `DrawerClose` disables the Button passed
  to `render`. So does `disabled` on that Button itself.
- **A name.** `DrawerTitle` names the sheet. With no title, pass `aria-label` to
  `DrawerPopup`.
- **A text close.** `<DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>} />`.
  A `DrawerClose` with nothing in it is one more x.
- **First focus.** It lands on the sheet itself, and Tab goes to its first control.
  `initialFocus` on `DrawerPopup` starts on the first control instead.
- **Focus back.** It returns to the trigger, after a swipe too.
- **A long text.** While `DrawerBody` scrolls it is a tab stop, so the keyboard reaches a
  text with no control in it. You write no `tabIndex`; `tabIndex={-1}` opts out.
- **A long action.** In the footer a label too long for one row wraps onto two lines.
- **Escape.** It closes one thing: a tooltip open inside the sheet first, then the sheet.
- **A phone.** The sheet pads the notch and the home indicator on the screen edges it
  touches. A phone reports them only to a page whose viewport meta has `viewport-fit=cover`.
- **A keyboard on a phone.** Every sheet scrolls the field you type in clear of it.
- **A new placement while open.** A side sheet on a desktop can become a bottom sheet on a
  phone while it is open: it stays the same sheet, with what was typed in it and the focus.
- **Arabic inside an English page.** The sheet takes its direction, its language and its
  swipe from the nearest `TopClassProvider`. Mount it: with none the sheet is laid out as
  the page is, but it swipes as a left-to-right page does.

### What Base UI gives

| Prop | On | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | `DrawerRoot` | Open state, yours or its own. |
| `modal` | `DrawerRoot` | How much of the page it blocks. See below. |
| `disablePointerDismissal` | `DrawerRoot` | A press outside no longer closes it. |
| `initialFocus`, `finalFocus` | `DrawerPopup` | Where focus goes on open and on close. |
| `container`, `keepMounted` | `DrawerPopup` | Where it mounts, and whether it stays mounted while closed. |
| `nativeButton` | `DrawerTrigger`, `DrawerClose` | `false` when `render` is not a button. |

- **`modal` (the default).** A scrim. The page takes no press, does not scroll and is hidden
  from a screen reader. Tab stays in the sheet.
- **`modal="trap-focus"`.** No scrim. The page takes presses and scrolls. Tab still stays in
  the sheet, and the page is still hidden from a screen reader.
- **`modal={false}`.** No scrim. The page takes presses, scrolls and is read. Tab past the
  x closes the sheet.
- **All three.** A press outside closes it, unless `disablePointerDismissal`. A swipe and
  the x close it always.
- **Why it closed.** `onOpenChange` gets `details.reason`: `'swipe'`, `'escape-key'`,
  `'close-press'` or `'outside-press'`. It needs a `'use client'` file.

### A form

A `form` with the class `contents` wraps the parts, so the submit button in the footer
belongs to it. Start it with a `DrawerHeader`: the room kept for the x does not reach
inside a `contents` form.

```tsx
<DrawerRoot placement="bottom">
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button>Invite</Button>} />
  <DrawerPopup>
    <form action={inviteTeammate} className="contents">
      <DrawerHeader>
        <DrawerTitle>Invite a teammate</DrawerTitle>
      </DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerBody>
        <Input name="email" type="email" aria-label="Email" fullWidth />
      </DrawerBody>
      <DrawerFooter>
        <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>} />
        <Button type="submit">Send</Button>
      </DrawerFooter>
    </form>
  </DrawerPopup>
</DrawerRoot>
```

- **From a server page.** Pass text, booleans, elements (`render={<Button />}`) and a
  Server Action. Pass no function: `onOpenChange`, a function `render`, a function
  `initialFocus` or `finalFocus`, and `actionsRef` need a `'use client'` file.
- **Not on the popup.** Do not write `render={<form />}` on `DrawerPopup`. It puts
  `role="dialog"` on a `form`, which HTML does not allow, and axe reports it.

### Not built

Snap points, the swipe that opens a closed sheet (Base UI's `SwipeArea`), the page that
shrinks behind a sheet (`Indent`), a style for a drawer inside a drawer, `dismissible`
(pass `disablePointerDismissal`), `swipeDirection` (it follows `placement`), and a trigger
outside its `DrawerRoot` (Base UI's `handle`: hold `open` in a client file instead).

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DrawerRoot,
  DrawerBody,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerPopup,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

### DrawerRoot

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger and the popup. With no trigger, hold `open` in a client file. |
| `placement` | no | `start` \| `end` \| `top` \| `bottom` | `"end"` | DrawerRoot: the edge the sheet slides from; start and end follow the direction. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | DrawerRoot: the widest a start or an end sheet grows, 256 to 480 px; custom sets no width. |

### DrawerBody

This part takes no design props of its own.

### DrawerClose

This part takes no design props of its own.

### DrawerHeader

This part takes no design props of its own.

### DrawerPopup

This part takes no design props of its own.

### DrawerTitle

This part takes no design props of its own.

### DrawerTrigger

This part takes no design props of its own.

`DrawerRoot` draws no element, so it takes no `className`, `style` or `ref`. Anything else on another part is passed to the element it draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
